sentences.text: Though these appeal are listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, they are taken up for final disposal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant Smt.Preeti Patil Melkundi, in MFA No.201893/2015 has submitted that Court below committed an error by not considering the evidence of RW1/official of company on the point that driver of the insured vehicle is not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and to substantiate, RW1 has marked documents at Exs.R-1 to R- 6,
which shows that legal notices issued to the driver and the owner of the jeep on the addresses furnished by themselves before the police as shown in the charge sheet and also in the insurance policy and both of them avoided accept the notice.
The driver of jeep and respondent No.2 herein clearly shows that the driver of the jeep was not holding driving licence.
Hence, they have intentionally avoided to take the notice.
Hence, they have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

4. Further it is submitted that tribunal has committed an error in awarding total compensation to the tune of Rs.9,70,000/- under different heads by considering the age of respondent no.1 as 18 years.
The documents on record at Ex.P-2 charge sheet, Ex.P-4 Wound certificate, Ex.P-6 disability certificate reveals that age of the injured was 15 years old at the time of accident.

In the case of minor injuries, the Apex Court in the case of MASTER MALLIKARJUN V. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, THE NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED & ANR. reported (2014) 14 SCC 396, is applicable to award compensation under conventional heads as mentioned therein.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED & ANR. reported (2014) 14 SCC 396
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On all these grounds sought for modification of the award and also exonerated the liability of the insurance company.
5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant in MFA No.200430/2016 has submitted his arguments that the compensation awarded is on lower side.
The tribunal ought to have awarded the compensation as claimed for after holding that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the jeep by its driver.
Tribunal has not awarded compensation in accordance with law and facts and also the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court.

Further it is submitted that the court below has awarded a sum of Rs.4,86,000/- towards loss of future earning by taking the income of the appellant at Rs.5,000/- and disability at 45% but the appellant is a salesman and earning a sum of Rs.5,000/- from the sales and he has lost earning capacity to the extent of 100% as he has lost his right amputated below thigh he cannot do his job.
Therefore the Court below has failed to consider the loss of earning at 100% and to calculate the loss of earning of the appellant as per the Exs.P-4 and P-5.
Further it is submitted that the tribunal has also not awarded just and proper compensation under other heads.
On all these grounds sought for allowing this appeal.

6. Further it is submitted b the learned counsel for the appellant that Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record as to the liability of the insurance company the IO has not Divisional Manager vs Sandeep S/O Monappa on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151339760/
3 submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the commission of offences punishable under Section 3 r/w 181 of MV act.

sentences.text: Respondents have not placed any materials to show that driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
On all these grounds sought for dismissal of the appeal filed b the insurance company.

7. Having heard the arguments on both sides and on perusal of records the following points would arise for consideration:
(1) Whether the appellant/claimant in MFA No.200430/2016 is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?
(2) Whether the appellant/insurance company has made out grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the multiplier taken by the Tribunal?
(3) Whether the appellant/insurance company has made out grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the insurance company?

(4) What order/award?
8.

My findings to the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : Partly Affirmative Point No.2 : in Affirmative Point No.3 : in Negative Point No.4 : as per final order:
9. The learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company has submitted her arguments that the documents on record Ex.P2/charge-sheet, P4/wound certificate,
P6/disability certificate reveal that the age of the injured was 15 years at the time of accident. But the Tribunal has taken the age as 18 years on the basis of discharge card, which is not correct.
10.

Today the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant has produced the copy of the identity card issued by the Election Commission of India, which reveals that the date of birth of injured is 06.08.1994.
The alleged accident took place on 15.03.2009.
Hence, the age of the injured was 14 years 4 months 9 days at the time of accident.

11. Relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121 and Divya vs The National Insurance Co. Ltd. & Anr. reported in 2022 Live Law (SC) 892 since the age of the injured was below 15 years, '15'
multiplier has to be taken into consideration, but the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the age of the injured as '18' years and taken multiplier as '18'
which is not correct.

Accordingly, I answered point No.2 in Affirmative.

12. The Tribunal has assessed the income of the petitioner at Rs.5,000/- and based on the medical evidence, the Tribunal has assessed the disability of petitioner to the extent of 45% to the whole body, which is just and proper and also in accordance with law.

13. In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kajal vs Jagdish Chand & Ors arising out of Civil Appeal No.735/2020 (arising out of SLP (C) No.15504/2019) 40% future prospects has to be added towards income of the petitioner, then it comes to Rs.7,000/- (5000+40%(2000)).

With these components, the loss of future earning works out to Rs.7,000/- x 12 x 15 x 45% =
Rs.5,67,000/- is awarded towards loss of future earning.

14. The learned counsel for appellant/claimant has relied on decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court - 10 - in 2023(1) SLC (Civil) 122 in Mohd. Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain vs Regional Manager, U.P.State Road Transport Corporation the compensation awarded towards pain & sufferings as Rs.2,00,000/-; loss of amenities Rs.2,00,000/-; and loss due to disability and disfigurement as Rs.2,00,000/- and seeks the same amount to the case hand.

sentences.text: 15. I have gone through the above judgment.
In that case the appellant has suffered 70% disability.

Taking into consideration of the facts and circumstances and also keeping in mind the above judgment relied by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant, it is just and proper to award compensation as under:

sentences.text: Thus, the petitioner is entitled compensation in a sum of Rs.10,61,000/- with interest at 6% p.a.
Accordingly, I answered point No.1 in partly Affirmative.

17. With regard to liability of insurance company is concerned, the Tribunal has observed in para-14 as under:
"14.

Having heard the argument of both the counsels, I have gone through the recitals of the above said decision, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has clearly observed the situations to exonerate the liability of the insurance company when the driver of the offending vehicle has been charge sheeted for the commission of offences U/s.3 of Motor Vehicle Act for having not possessed the valid Driving License.

When such being so, in this case the contents of the Charge sheet are not disclosing regarding the commission of offences by the driver of the offending vehicle by driving such vehicle without valid Driving License and he has not been charge sheeted for the offences punishable U/s 3 of Motor Vehicle Act.

Therefore, on keen observations of the above said decision it is not applicable to the case on hand,
wherein there are no any allegations against the driver of the Jeep regarding non holding of the valid Driving License to drive vehicle.
Moreover the Legal Notice and returned RPAD covers are revealing that, either the owner or the driver are not duly intimated to discharge their duty to produce the RC and Driving License.
Thus, there are no any sufficient evidence on the part of the 2nd respondent to believe that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the valid and effective Driving License.
Therefore, I am of the concluded opinion that, 2nd respondent has failed to prove this defence.

Hence, I answered this issue in the negative."
18.
The Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and - 12 - directed the insurance company to pay the award amount.
Hence, I do not find any ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the insurance company.

Hence, I answered point No.3 in Negative.
19.

For the aforesaid reasons discussed, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) MFA No.200430/2016 filed by appellant/claimant is allowed in part.
ii) MFA No.201893/2015 filed by appellant/insurance company is allowed in part.
